subject: Re: Stellaris: rights & model-use — proposed compromise and next steps
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@stellaris.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom@stellaris.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Stellaris MSA + Order Form (marked) — ownership & training concerns

Marcus — attaching our marked-up MSA and the order form. High-level asks from legal:

1) Output ownership: Stellaris expects an express assignment of rights to outputs produced by the Service when those outputs are generated from our prompts and data. We would like a clause that makes clear Stellaris owns the output and Redwood has no right to reuse.

2) Training / feedback: We cannot allow any use of our inputs or outputs to train public or internal models without explicit, opt-in written consent. We are open to a limited, internal-only feedback license for operations & quality improvement that is non-commercial, but only if it is scoped, timeboxed, and deletable on request.

3) Attribution / branding: Any marketing use of Stellaris output or case studies must receive prior written approval.

We left inline comments and suggested wording in the PDF (see attachment). Please confirm receipt and let us know an estimated timeline for a response.

Attachments: Stellaris_MSA_markedup_20270315.pdf (PDF, 3 pages with inline redlines)

Best,
Elena

Elena — thanks, we received the PDF and have started an internal review. High-level acknowledgment and plan:

- We understand the core asks (output ownership, strict no-training, marketing approvals).
- We need to balance Stellaris' requirements with our platform model: Redwood's standard approach is to grant customers broad rights to outputs while reserving a narrow feedback license for quality and safety improvements.
- Immediate next steps: Neha will propose legal compromise language; Aditya will assess technical feasibility for: a) enforceable opt-out of training, b) isolated telemetry retention and deletion windows, and c) options for an escrow/blackbox approach if needed.

Timeline: expect a proposed redline package and internal commentary by EOD Thursday (2027-03-18). If there are urgent gating items (procurement deadline), flag them and we'll prioritise.

Marcus

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stellaris MSA + Order Form (marked) — tech notes on training opt-out

Quick technical readout to inform negotiation:

- Opt-out for training: We can implement a strict opt-out at the tenant level so Stellaris data is never written to training corpora or to long-term feature stores. This requires tagging all request telemetry and ensuring our feedback pipeline filters based on that tag. Implementation ETA: 2-3 weeks for complete auditability + deletion hooks; 1 week for an operational 'opt-out' flag (non-audited).

- Deletion/retention: We can add a 30/90/365 day retention option that is enforceable. For deletion-on-request we will need a documented process and SLA (e.g., 48-72 hours for purging ephemeral logs; longer for backups).

- Narrow feedback license: technical carveouts we can support: aggregated model diagnostics, anomaly detection, safety signals, and latency/quality metrics (non-document-level). We cannot provide customer-level example reuse for commercial model training if the contract prohibits it.

- Model escrow/blackbox: If Stellaris wants guarantees around reproducibility without Redwood retaining data, we can discuss an escrow of a frozen model snapshot generated under their tenancy. That increases complexity and cost (storage + legal controls).

Happy to join a call with Stellaris legal/engineering to walk through the implementation detail.

— Aditya

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stellaris MSA + Order Form (marked) — proposed compromise language

Team — drafted compromise language that tries to preserve Redwood's ability to improve the service while meeting Stellaris' privacy and IP asks. Key points below and attached as tracked changes (.docx):

1) Outputs: Add a clause in the Order Form: "Customer is the owner of Outputs, defined as text, images or other artifacts generated solely in response to Customer prompts. Redwood grants no rights in Customer Outputs except as necessary to provide the Service." This gives Stellaris clear ownership while allowing Redwood to operate the service.

2) Feedback license: Introduce a narrow, non-exclusive, royalty-free, revocable license limited to aggregated, de-identified telemetry and quality signals for the purpose of service improvement and safety. Explicitly exclude use of Customer Inputs or Outputs for model training unless Customer provides written opt-in for specified use-cases and term.

3) Opt-out & deletion: Provide a contract right for tenant-level opt-out (effective within 14 days of activation) and a documented deletion SLA: 72 hours for primary stores, 30 days for backups. Include an audit clause (Redwood provides quarterly attestation of compliance for the retention policy).

4) Marketing & attribution: Add a standard marketing carve-out requiring prior written approval for using Customer Outputs or naming the Customer in case studies.

5) Escrow option: Offer an optional add-on: periodic model snapshot escrow under a neutral custodian with separate fees and operational runbook.

I recommend we propose: (a) accept customer ownership of Outputs, (b) carve out a narrowly drafted feedback license as described, and (c) offer escrow and tighter retention as paid options. This aligns with our platform guarantees while preserving product-led improvements.

I'll attach the tracked-change MSA and a clean Order Form with the above positions. If you agree, I'll prepare a cover email and a single-doc redline for Stellaris.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@stellaris.ai>, Tom Hayes <tom@stellaris.ai>, legal@stellaris.ai

Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Stellaris — proposed redlines and next steps

Elena / Stellaris team — thanks for the marked-up MSA and patience while we reviewed. Attached are three documents: a tracked MSA with our suggested compromise, a clean Order Form reflecting the Outputs/opt-out language, and a short one-page summary of technical controls and operational SLAs.

Summary of the key commercial positions we propose:
- Customer ownership of Outputs: we accept explicit Customer ownership of Outputs generated solely from Customer prompts and data.
- Feedback license: Redwood requests a narrow, revocable license limited to aggregated, de-identified telemetry and quality signals for the sole purpose of improving service quality and safety. No document-level reuse; no model training from Customer Inputs or Outputs without Customer opt-in.
- Opt-out & deletion: Tenant-level opt-out available. Deletion SLA: 72 hours for primary stores; up to 30 days for removing items from backups. Quarterly attestation available for an enterprise add-on.
- Escrow: Optional paid model snapshot escrow available as an add-on; we included preliminary pricing in the Order Form.
- Marketing: Redwood will not use Customer Outputs or identify Customer in marketing collateral without prior written consent.

Next steps: please review attached redlines and confirm 3 windows next week for a 30-45 minute call (legal + engineering) to finalize the wording. If those positions are acceptable in principle, we can generate a single clean MSA + order form for signature within 48 hours of the call.

Attachments: proposed-redlines-20270320.docx, Stellaris_OrderForm_clean_20270320.docx, technical-controls-summary-20270320.pdf

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
